newsitem.title: PHILIPPINES: Manila bourse cancels trading after power failure.
newsitem.headline: Manila bourse cancels trading after power failure.

text.p: * Official says trading to resume Tuesday
The Philippine Stock Exchange (PSE) had decided to cancel trading for the day after a power failure crippled the electronic trading system, an official said on Monday.
"But we guarantee that tomorrow we will be online one way or another," PSE governor Ramon Garcia told a local television station.
Brokers said they expected trading to remain sluggish on Tuesday due to a lack of market moving developments.
On Friday, the Philippine Stock Exchange composite index had risen by 17.11 points to 2,944.48
The bourse's board of governors will meet at noon (0400 GMT) to thresh out the problem which hit one of its trading floors, chief operating officer Rafael Llave told Reuters.
The Philippine bourse operates out of two floors, one in Ayala Tower in Manila's Makati business district and another in the Tektite building located in the alternate business district, Ortigas.
A total power failure hit the Tektite building, Llave said.
The Tektite building administrator had not yet explained why there was no electricity in the building. Power generators also failed due to overheating, he said.
"The Tektite tower is uninhabitable ... There's no airconditioning," Llave said.

The Philippine Stock Exchange has had several trading suspensions in the past mainly due to either computer or telecommmunications breakdown. But this is the first time trading has been cancelled because of a power failure.
